newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL interbank rates steady in thin trading.
newsitem.headline: KL interbank rates steady in thin trading.

text.p: Interbank rates were steady on Friday in thin trading with both borrowers and lenders largely sidelined, dealers said.
The market was closed on Thursday for a national holiday and they said players were only expected back after the weekend.
"Rates are still holding but there's not much activity," said a dealer with a Malaysian bank.
One-week money was at 7.00/10 percent, two-week at 7.10/20 percent and three-week at 7.20/30 percent, all about unchanged from Wednesday's levels.
One-month money was steady at 7.25/30 percent, three-month at 7.35/40 percent against 7.30/35 and six-month at 7.40/45 percent from 7.35/40.
The overnight interbank rate was expected to ease slightly due to maturity of Bank Negara bills worth 500 million ringgit on Friday, dealers said. It closed at 6.50/70 percent on Wednesday.
The maturity, however, was likely to have little impact as the market was supported at the current levels, partly due to reduced activity.
Dealers said they expected the central bank to call for a fresh Bank Negara bill issue next week.
Dealers said there was also a persistent rumour about a possible long-term government bond issue soon to roll over maturing bonds. The rumour has prevented lenders from lending lower, they said.
A 900-million ringgit long-term government bond issue will mature on May 15.
Interest rate futures on the Malaysia Monetary Exchange were mixed.
At 0500 GMT, the benchmark three-month Kuala Lumpur Interbank Offered Rate (KLIBOR) September contract was down one point to 92.67, or an implied yield of 7.33 percent.
June and December were both unchanged at 92.67, or 7.33 percent while March 1998 was up one point to 92.61, or 7.39 percent.
